chunks: Ask them about the town that was by the sea, when they transgressed on the Sabbath, when their fish came to them sprawling on the surface, and on the day they did not keep the Sabbath they did not come to them. Thus We tested them for what they used to be disobedient.

key_terms.شُرَّعًا: sprawling / coming to the surface easily

ai.seo_question: What is the story of the town by the sea mentioned in Surah Al-A'raf regarding the Sabbath?
ai.summary: This verse (7:163) highlights the divine test of the coastal community, where fish surfaced abundantly on the Sabbath but remained elusive on other days, symbolizing how God rewards obedience with ease and punishes transgression with difficulty. Shia scholars often interpret this as a lesson in maintaining ritual purity and discipline, warning against the corruption that arises when religious observance becomes a means of worldly gain rather than spiritual devotion. The narrative serves as a precursor to the broader theme of prophetic succession and the consequences of deviating from divine commandments.
